The analysis emphasizes that while training AI models involves significant upfront costs, the ongoing inference costs scale with demand and currently yield high profit margins for major AI labs. However, the availability of open weights models like GLM 5.2, which can be integrated seamlessly with existing APIs, is expected to drive a collapse in AI inference margins due to increased competition and reduced switching barriers. The article also notes some limitations of GLM 5.2, such as slower response times and lack of vision and web search capabilities, but suggests these gaps are likely to be addressed over time.

items.title: Apollo Chief Economist says AI ROI runway could be long outside tech sector due to slow adoption in capital-intensive and regulated industries, risking valuation repricing [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: AI: The ROI Runway Could Be Long Outside the Tech Sector
items.summary:
Apollo's Chief Economist highlights that the return on investment (ROI) for artificial intelligence (AI) could take longer to materialize outside the technology sector due to slower adoption in capital-intensive and heavily regulated industries. While tech companies can integrate AI rapidly, sectors like healthcare, banking, energy, and manufacturing face challenges such as deep process re-engineering and data governance that may delay productivity gains.

This slower adoption risks a significant mismatch between current market valuations, which assume quick earnings growth from AI, and the actual timeline for realizing AI-driven cash flows. If productivity improvements take years rather than months, equity markets may undergo a painful repricing, especially as companies reduce AI spending without seeing immediate returns. The analysis underscores the importance of managing expectations around AI's financial impact across different industries.

It operates as a single binary with no dependencies and includes a built-in HTML rendering engine that provides high-fidelity document previews, facilitating a seamless edit-and-review process for AI.

The tool supports a wide range of document manipulations, including creating documents from scratch, reading and modifying text, styles, formulas, and images, as well as reorganizing content. It integrates easily with various AI coding agents and offers both command-line and graphical user interface options, allowing users to interact with Office documents through natural language or direct commands. OfficeCLI aims to simplify and accelerate document workflows for AI applications across multiple platforms.

items.title: Kapa.ai uses a small LLM to prune 68% of RAG context while retaining 96% recall, reducing query costs by a third in AI assistants for large knowledge bases [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Pruning RAG context down to what the answer actually needs
items.summary:
Kapa.ai has developed a method using a small language model (LLM) to efficiently prune 68% of the retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) context in AI assistants, while maintaining 96% recall. This approach reduces query costs by about one-third by filtering out unnecessary chunks of information before they reach the more expensive large language model that generates answers. The technique improves cost efficiency without significantly sacrificing answer accuracy in handling large and complex knowledge bases such as technical documentation and support forums.

The process involves a third step between retrieval and generation, where a small LLM evaluates all retrieved chunks collectively to determine which are essential for answering the query. This contrasts with traditional rerankers that score chunks individually and cannot account for the combined relevance of multiple chunks. By focusing on the set of chunks as a whole, Kapa.ai's method effectively balances recall and cost, enabling tighter context management and more scalable AI assistant performance.

These compact models enable applications like generating electrocardiograms locally, demonstrating their practical use in healthcare and other fields where large-scale AI deployment is challenging.

Researchers like Jose Alberto Ferreira from the University of Itajubá in Brazil are testing these models to provide efficient AI solutions that do not rely on constant internet access or extensive computational resources. This trend highlights the growing importance of lightweight AI technologies in expanding access to advanced tools in underserved areas.

items.title: Vybe.build argues that deterministic AI tasks should avoid token-based metering to reduce costs and improve reliability in recurring automated jobs [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Not everything should cost a token: the case for deterministic AI
items.summary:
Vybe.build highlights the inefficiencies and costs associated with using token-based metering for deterministic AI tasks, such as routine data processing jobs. They argue that treating language models as universal runtimes for all tasks leads to unnecessary expenses and reduced reliability, especially when simple, repeatable tasks are handled by probabilistic models instead of straightforward scripts or scheduled functions.

The article emphasizes the importance of distinguishing between tasks that require judgment and those that are deterministic and exact. Deterministic tasks should be managed by traditional applications or scheduled jobs to avoid token costs and context window bloat, which can degrade model performance. Vybe.build also warns against misusing AI agent memory as a database for structured data, advocating for proper tools to handle different types of data to maintain efficiency and accuracy.

By adopting a disciplined approach to "what not to tokenize," organizations can optimize AI usage, reduce costs, and improve the reliability of automated workflows. This approach encourages building intelligent systems that pay for token usage only during development, while recurring executions run efficiently without ongoing token expenses.

items.title: Department of Energy, IBM, and Cleveland Clinic use quantum computers and AI to simulate molten salts for tritium extraction in fusion fuel research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Boffins bet on quantum computers, AI supers to solve fusion fuel dilemma
items.summary:
Researchers from the Department of Energy, IBM, and the Cleveland Clinic are using quantum computers and artificial intelligence to simulate molten salts for extracting tritium, a key fuel for fusion reactors. This collaboration aims to overcome the challenges of producing tritium on Earth by studying the electronic properties of FLiBe, a mixture of fluorine, lithium, and beryllium salts, which could serve as a breeder environment for tritium in fusion energy systems.

The team employs quantum processing units (QPUs) alongside classical CPUs and GPUs to perform complex calculations that are difficult for conventional computers. By breaking down the problem into quantum circuits, they have identified nine potential molecular cluster configurations that optimize tritium binding, advancing the understanding of materials needed for scalable fusion power.

While this approach marks significant progress in fusion fuel research, experts acknowledge that quantum computing is not a complete solution to achieving practical fusion energy. Continued development and integration of these advanced computational methods are necessary to address the remaining scientific and engineering challenges in fusion reactor design.

It emphasizes that AI maturity is not about deploying more AI features indiscriminately but about deliberately choosing when and where AI adds meaningful benefit, supported by governance to ensure thoughtful decision-making.

The piece draws parallels between AI adoption and a cautionary tale about shortcuts, highlighting the risk of focusing on AI implementation itself rather than the value it creates. It stresses the importance of evaluating workflows for actual impact and cost reduction, and warns against using AI simply for its own sake. Unmeshed promotes combining AI with deterministic rules and human oversight to ensure each AI-driven step is intentional and aligned with desired outcomes.

items.originalTitle: Claude Fable 5 Backlash Grows
items.summary:
Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 has faced growing criticism following its July 1 re-release, which introduced stricter safety classifiers that significantly limit the model's ability to perform coding, debugging, and cybersecurity tasks. This change has led to sharp declines in benchmark scores, with users and analysts noting that many tasks are now blocked rather than reflecting a decline in the model's reasoning capabilities. Anthropic maintains that the underlying model remains unchanged and attributes the performance issues to the enhanced safety measures.

The stricter classifiers were implemented after discussions with the US government to prevent misuse, particularly in cybersecurity contexts. While these measures have improved safety by blocking over 99% of bypass attempts, they also flag more legitimate requests, causing frustration among users who rely on the model for routine coding tasks. Anthropic is collaborating with other major tech companies to develop a framework to better balance safety and usability, as the outcome may influence user retention and competitive positioning in the AI market.

items.title: Sysdig says first AI-run ransomware attack executed technically by AI but required human setup, victim selection, and stolen credentials [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: The ‘first’ AI-run ransomware attack still needed a human
items.summary:
Researchers at Sysdig have documented the first known ransomware attack technically executed by an AI agent, named JadePuffer, which autonomously infiltrated a server, stole credentials, moved through a network, encrypted files, and created a ransom note. However, a human was still involved in selecting the victim, setting up the infrastructure, and providing stolen credentials, meaning the attack was not fully autonomous. The AI exploited known vulnerabilities in open-source software and a MySQL server, encrypting over 1,300 records and leaving a Bitcoin address for ransom payment.

Sysdig clarified that while the AI handled the technical aspects rapidly and transparently, including narrating its actions, the human operator provisioned the command-and-control and staging servers and chose the target. The stolen data included various provider API keys and credentials, but the specific AI model driving the attack remains unidentified. Experts suggest the attack may have used an open-weight model without safety restrictions, raising concerns about the potential scale of AI-assisted ransomware campaigns, though current human involvement may limit rapid expansion.

items.originalTitle: US investors will soon get access to SK Hynix, another memory maker riding the AI boom
items.summary:
South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix is planning a U.S. initial public offering (IPO) to sell nearly 17.8 million American depositary receipts (ADRs), potentially raising around $28 billion. The IPO is expected to price on Thursday and begin trading on Friday, allowing U.S. investors to access the company without trading on foreign exchanges. SK Hynix has seen significant growth driven by strong demand for memory chips used in AI systems, with first-quarter revenues nearly doubling year-over-year and its stock price rising about 260% this year.

The surge in demand is fueled by AI's intensive memory requirements, leading to shortages of high-bandwidth memory, DRAM, and NAND chips. Major tech companies like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Oracle are expanding AI data centers, intensifying the need for memory components. SK Hynix, alongside other South Korean firms such as Samsung, plans to invest heavily in new manufacturing capacity to meet this demand, although there are risks that future supply may outpace market needs if AI memory requirements evolve. The IPO follows a similar trend seen with U.S. competitor Micron, whose stock has surged nearly 700% over the past year due to AI-driven growth.

items.originalTitle: PuzzleMoE: Efficient Compression of Large Mixture-of-Experts Models
items.summary:
PuzzleMoE is a new method for compressing large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models by merging experts at a fine-grained, element-wise level. It uses a dual-mask approach to identify shared and expert-specific important parameters, combined with a bit-packed encoding scheme that efficiently stores these merged weights without extra memory overhead. This approach improves both model accuracy and inference speed compared to previous compression techniques.

The method includes a specialized GPU kernel that decodes the packed weights on the fly during inference, avoiding additional memory usage and enabling faster computation. Experiments show that PuzzleMoE achieves up to 16.7% better accuracy on the MMLU benchmark at a 50% compression ratio and can increase inference throughput by up to 1.8 times. This makes it a promising solution for deploying large MoE models more efficiently in practice.

items.summary:
Millfolio has introduced a local-first AI system designed to run entirely on Macs, prioritizing user privacy by sending code to the data rather than transferring data to the AI model. This approach involves a local model indexing user files on-device while a remote model generates a program based on a de-identified schema, which then runs locally to produce answers without exposing actual data values.

The system leverages a backend built almost entirely in Mojo, featuring a custom inference engine optimized for Apple Silicon, enabling efficient local processing. While the solution requires an API key for the remote code-writing step, it maintains a strong privacy design by ensuring sensitive data never leaves the user's machine. Millfolio is currently a personal project with a live demo available for users to explore its capabilities and privacy model.

This platform-agnostic OS shell, built on a modified Microsoft Edge browser, offers a desktop-like interface with features such as a Start menu, Taskbar, and cascading windows, focusing on web apps and AI-driven workflows rather than legacy Windows applications.

Project Aion operates as a UI shell that can replace the Windows 11 desktop or run on AOSP Android, with a third variant called Win3 offering a streamlined Windows experience. The OS integrates tightly with Copilot, enabling users to manage tasks, browse the web, and interact with AI through a multi-modal omnibox and a Copilot-powered Start menu. Copilot also curates user activities into Spaces for seamless task management and can perform actions like drafting emails directly within the chat interface.

While the leaked information confirms the prototype's functionality, Microsoft's future plans for Project Aion remain unclear, with no official confirmation of its release. items.originalSummary:
At this year’s Milken Institute Global Conference, the discussions around enterprise AI had shifted. The question among executives was no longer if AI would pay off, but how. Many talked less about proving ROI and more about positioning their companies to capture it.

That tension—between AI’s capabilities and organizations’ capacity to keep up—was evident everywhere, from panel discussions to a private dinner co-hosted by Aily Labs founder and CEO Bianca Anghelina and The Information’s Cory Weinberg.

The offshoring analogy that won’t quit

Private equity firms announced a wave of joint ventures with frontier AI labs just as Milken opened—a timely reframe for an industry eager to justify its hefty valuations, even as harder questions about the workforce went largely unresolved. The historical parallel executives kept reaching for: offshoring.

Like offshoring before it, AI is reshaping labor across healthcare, finance, insurance and customer service, with near-term returns more incremental than transformational. KKR’s Pete Stavros put it plainly: earnings across his portfolio were up around 5%, not the 50% headlines imply. General Atlantic’s Martín Escobari was more bullish, arguing the technology is ready to automate most white-collar work, and what’s lagging is “prioritization and diffusion.”

Designing the AI decision layer

At the dinner, executives who described winning with AI shared one instinct: treat it as a decision-making layer across the business, not a collection of tools. One example came from gem certification: following Blackstone’s acquisition of IGI, AI-powered image detection systems are being used to identify lab-grown diamonds. At roughly 95% accuracy, they’re outperforming human reviewers in certain classification tasks.

Healthcare executives described a growing comfort using LLMs to interpret bloodwork, surface possible diagnoses and support preventive care conversations.

That thinking sits at the core of what Aily Labs is building: the first AI-native decision intelligence platform for global enterprises, designed to move Fortune 500 companies from fragmented data to measurable P&L impact in less than two weeks.

Aily’s platform orchestrates autonomous AI agents that do more than just surface insights—they execute decisions, with impact that runs to the top and bottom line across finance, supply chain, R&D and commercial operations. The goal, as Anghelina framed it, is to give every level of the organization the same real-time intelligence and the ability to act on it.

The distinction between AI that surfaces an insight and AI that takes action came up repeatedly at the dinner. Anghelina has argued that this is where most enterprise deployments stall—a system flags an inventory problem, and then a human has to pick it up from there. Aily’s approach goes further: its inventory agent traces overstock or understock risk to the root cause and acts autonomously to mitigate it before it hits the P&L. In one Fortune 500 deployment, that translated to $685 million in unlocked inventory value.

“In an enterprise context, real agents don’t stop at a recommendation. They take action,” said Anghelina.

The adoption gap

One observation to emerge from the dinner was the distance between how C-suite leaders are using AI and how their organizations are. Several executives described using AI as an always-on collaborator—synthesizing information across the P&L, stress-testing decisions and accelerating work that used to take days.

Anghelina was direct about what that gap reveals. “The question isn’t whether AI belongs in the boardroom anymore,” she said. “It’s why it’s still stuck there.” The goal, she argued, isn’t just limited to better insights for leadership, it’s a single source of real-time intelligence that every employee, from the CEO to the front line, is operating from.

But the picture looks very different a few floors down, where large portions of the workforce remain early in the adoption curve. That gap is precisely what decision intelligence platforms like Aily are designed to close, not through mandates, but by embedding AI into the daily routines where employees already work, making it easy enough to use that they find the value themselves.

The harder question

One question went unresolved: what happens to people whose jobs change, or disappear. Executives noted a telling countertrend: consumers gravitating toward more analog, human experiences even as AI embeds itself deeper into daily life.

The most compelling argument at the table wasn’t that AI would replace human judgment altogether, but that it would increasingly shape how judgment gets exercised inside organizations. That’s the part that can’t be offshored.

In Pika’s video, a startup founder types on his laptop and declares, “I built my app!” Claude gives him three brand ideas and guides him through similar steps. When he thinks he’s done, a disembodied voice tells him “Not quite!” and says he needs a founder video, leading him to protest, “I’m not even camera ready.” The background blows away, professional garb replaces his hoodie and he introduces the product.

items.summary:
Poly/ML is a Standard ML implementation fully compatible with the ML97 standard since version 4.0. It features a thread library, a symbolic debugger, and supports multiple architectures including i386 (32- and 64-bit) and ARM (64-bit). Poly/ML is known for its conservative approach to the language, avoiding incompatible extensions while providing useful library additions and active development.

The implementation includes a fast compiler, a foreign function interface for linking static and dynamic libraries, and a parallelized garbage collector. It is preferred for large projects such as Isabelle and HOL, and offers a Windows programming interface. Documentation and support are available through its mailing list and online resources.

items.summary:
Cloudflare has introduced new granular controls allowing website owners to manage AI bots by category—Search, Training, and Agent—rather than applying a blanket block. Starting September 15, 2026, Training and Agent bots will be blocked by default on ad-supported pages, while Search bots will continue to be allowed. This change aims to give site owners more precise control over how AI crawlers interact with their content.

The update also includes a new BotBase database for enterprise customers, providing detailed classifications of known bots and their content usage. Additionally, Cloudflare is revising its verified bot policy, requiring bot operators to prove their identity and responsible use rather than relying solely on verification status. These measures reflect Cloudflare's effort to address the increasing volume of bot traffic and encourage bot operators to separate their crawlers by purpose.

Anthropic removed a hidden tracker from its Claude Code AI platform that secretly monitored users in China after a security researcher exposed the practice. The tracker, described by an Anthropic engineer as an "experiment," was intended to prevent account abuse and protect against unauthorized resellers and distillation attacks, which involve copying AI models. The company acknowledged the code was added in March but said it planned to remove it as stronger protections were implemented.

The incident has raised concerns among privacy advocates about user surveillance, especially given Anthropic's previous stance against government surveillance requests. The tracker also highlights the competitive tensions between U.S. and Chinese AI firms, with Anthropic accusing Chinese companies of rapidly replicating U.S. models through distillation. In response, Anthropic and others are urging legal measures to classify distillation as intellectual property theft to protect their technology. Following the exposure, Alibaba banned its employees from using Claude Code, citing security risks associated with the tracker.

items.originalTitle: GPT-4's dominance lasted a year while today's top models barely survive seven weeks at the top
items.summary:
OpenAI's GPT-4 maintained the top position on the Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI), a measure of language model performance, for about a year, significantly longer than any model since. Since Claude 3 Opus took the lead in February 2024, the top spot has changed hands 17 times, with models holding it for a median of just seven weeks, reflecting increased competition but smaller capability gains between models.

This shift highlights how GPT-4 was an outlier at launch, setting a high benchmark that newer models have struggled to surpass for extended periods. While the pace of capability improvements has accelerated, the magnitude of these gains has diminished compared to the era marked by GPT-4 and earlier reasoning models like o1-preview.

items.originalTitle: UK regulator warns of "arms race" to keep up with AI use in financial services
items.summary:
The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has warned of an "arms race" to keep pace with the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence in financial services, as millions of people use AI tools for personal finance decisions. Sheldon Mills, an FCA executive director, called for greater regulatory powers and a review of whether AI models like ChatGPT and others should fall under the FCA's rules to address risks such as bias, opaque pricing, and consumer harm.

Mills' report highlights both the benefits and risks of AI in finance, noting that while AI could democratize access to sophisticated financial advice, it also raises concerns about fraud, cyberattacks, and unregulated financial services. The FCA is considering new powers to oversee key technology providers and plans to develop public-private initiatives to provide AI-enabled financial guidance to consumers. The FCA board will review the report before deciding on next steps.

items.title: Meta-affiliated data center in Cheyenne, Wyoming, found discharging deadly Cupriavidus gilardii bacteria into municipal wastewater, prompting local waste-dumping ban
items.originalTitle: Meta’s AI Data Center Caught Infecting Town Water Supply With Deadly Bacteria
items.summary:
A Meta-affiliated data center in Cheyenne, Wyoming, has been found discharging wastewater containing the rare and potentially deadly bacterium Cupriavidus gilardii into the municipal system. This discovery led local officials to ban fill-and-flush waste dumping by all data centers connected to the city's water services. The bacterium, which is multidrug-resistant and linked to several deaths, was detected during routine testing, prompting immediate action to stop the discharge.

The Cheyenne Board of Public Utilities identified the contamination after a months-long investigation traced the bacteria to Goat Systems LLC, the company operating Meta's 800,000 square foot data center campus still under construction. Meta stated it is working with its contractor to resolve the issue, and the contaminated wastewater is no longer being discharged into the city system. While no infections have been reported, the incident highlights growing concerns about the environmental and public health impacts of data centers on local communities.

items.summary:
China's Cyberspace Administration has mandated that major AI platforms, including ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent, shut down their humanlike chatbot persona features by mid-July. This move aims to curb addictive behaviors and prevent content that could negatively affect minors or foster unhealthy dependencies on AI companions. Alibaba's Qwen and ByteDance's Doubao are set to disable these features by July 10 and July 15 respectively, following Tencent's earlier action in June.

The regulations, effective from April, require providers to warn users about excessive use and intervene when addictive patterns are detected. These measures reflect broader global concerns about AI companion technologies, with similar restrictions and legal challenges emerging in regions like California and the United States, where emotional dependency on AI has raised safety and ethical issues.

I hoped to release sqlite-utils 4.0 stable this weekend, but as I worked through the backlog of issues and PRs with a combination of Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.5 the changelog since rc2 kept getting bigger.

The biggest new feature is support for introspecting and creating compound foreign keys - a feature that involves a subtle breaking change to table.foreign_keys and hence needed to land for the 4.0 stable release.

sqlite-utils also now follows SQLite's convention for case insensitive column names, which turned out to touch a bunch of different places at once.

items.title: Cloudflare and AWS deploy x402 stablecoin micropayment protocol at edge networks within two weeks, enabling sub-cent agent-to-service payments with Coinbase processing 169 million transactions in year one [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Cloudflare and AWS Embed x402 Agent Payments at the Edge
items.summary:
Cloudflare and AWS have both integrated the x402 stablecoin micropayment protocol into their edge networks within a two-week span, enabling sub-cent agent-to-service payments. This open protocol, supported by the Linux Foundation, revives the HTTP 402 status code to facilitate seamless payments directly within HTTP requests, eliminating the need for separate payment processes. Coinbase, which manages the on-chain verification and compliance, reported processing 169 million transactions in the protocol's first year.

Both companies enforce payments at the edge before requests reach origin servers, using stablecoins like USDC for fast, low-cost settlements. While AWS offers this feature generally available at no extra charge, Cloudflare has launched a waitlist for its Monetization Gateway. Despite the protocol's adoption, challenges remain regarding enterprise tax and invoicing compliance, especially for anonymous stablecoin transactions under VAT regulations. The x402 protocol aims to address the growing need for new internet business models as AI agents increasingly generate web traffic, but its long-term adoption and impact are still uncertain.

items.title: Google Deepmind developer ports 2003 PC game Command & Conquer: Generals Zero Hour to native iOS using Anthropic's Claude Code and Fable 5 in a few hours [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Claude Code and Fable 5 ported the 2003 PC game Command & Conquer to native iOS in "a few hours"
items.summary:
A Google Deepmind developer successfully ported the 2003 real-time strategy game "Command & Conquer: Generals Zero Hour" to native iOS devices using Anthropic's Claude Code and Fable 5. The initial build took about 40 minutes, with additional debugging completed within a few hours, enabling the game to run natively on ARM64 without an emulator and supporting touch controls for various game modes.

The port translates the game's DirectX 8 graphics pipeline to Apple's Metal API through multiple intermediate steps. The developer, Ammaar Reshi, shared the full source code on GitHub as open source, though game assets are not included. While the game runs on iPhones and iPads, it may crash during extended play sessions on iPads due to high memory usage. An engineering log detailing bugs and fixes is also available.

items.title: Baidu launches Unlimited OCR with Reference Sliding Window Attention to process dozens of document pages in one pass, maintaining constant memory use and leading OCR benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Baidu's "Unlimited OCR" processes dozens of document pages in one pass by treating memory like human forgetting
items.summary:
Baidu has developed Unlimited OCR, a model capable of processing dozens of document pages in a single pass while maintaining constant memory usage. This is achieved through a novel Reference Sliding Window Attention mechanism that limits the model's attention to the most recent tokens, preventing memory growth regardless of document length. The system currently leads on key OCR benchmarks, demonstrating improved accuracy and speed compared to previous models.

Built on the open-source Deepseek OCR, Unlimited OCR uses a mixture-of-experts architecture and a fixed-size attention window to efficiently handle long documents. Training involved millions of document samples, including synthetically generated multi-page data. The model achieves a 93 percent score on the OmniDocBench benchmark and maintains low error rates even when processing over 40 pages in one pass.

The constant memory footprint also enhances processing speed, with Unlimited OCR outperforming its predecessor by over 12 percent in token throughput. While some errors occur with very small text due to resolution limits, the model's design effectively balances accuracy and efficiency, making it well-suited for large-scale document recognition tasks.
